claims.wording: Cocktail is Maintain's macOS maintenance utility.
claims.excerpt: Cocktail is a general-purpose utility for macOS that lets you clean, repair, and optimize your Mac.
claims.conditions: Clean/repair/optimize is vendor positioning, not a measured result.

claims.wording: The official page lists 20.2.2 Golden Gate Edition (macOS 27), 19.10.1 Tahoe Edition (macOS 26), and 18.9 Sequoia Edition (macOS 15).
claims.excerpt: Golden Gate Edition (macOS 27) v. 20.2.2 / Tahoe Edition (macOS 26) v. 19.10.1 / Sequoia Edition (macOS 15) v. 18.9
claims.conditions: Exact vendor labels only, not independently verified Apple release names, binary versions or tested OS compatibility. Feature parity across editions unknown.

claims.wording: The official page documents cache/log maintenance, database rebuilding, Spotlight and Time Machine controls, network settings, and Finder/Dock customization.
claims.excerpt: Clear system, user, Internet and applications caches / Clear and manage (view, print and save) log files / Rebuild Launch Services, Help and Accessibility databases / Manage Spotlight indexing / Thin or delete Time Machine snapshots / Change speed, duplex and MTU of network cards / Customize look and features of Finder, Dock, login window and other system services
claims.conditions: Catalogue is not edition-specific validation; not advice to execute all tasks, disable protections, remove snapshots or change memory settings.

claims.wording: Pilot is documented for one-button maintenance and scheduling cache/log clearing and critical security-update enforcement.
claims.excerpt: Perform essential system maintenance; clean, repair and optimize your system with one click of the button / Schedule clearing of caches and log files as well as enforcement of critical security updates
claims.conditions: Exact schedule, login/runtime requirements, previews, per-path approvals and reversibility not established.

claims.wording: Unregistered Cocktail expires after its fifth launch; licences cover current editions, with earlier-edition licences available on request at no additional charge.
claims.excerpt: When unregistered, Cocktail runs in demo mode and will expire after the fifth launch. / Your license will be valid for all current editions of Cocktail, and you will also be able to request a license (without any additional charge) for any previous edition by contacting us.
claims.conditions: Do not infer unlimited days, future-major-version upgrades, perpetual entitlement, open-source licensing or refund terms.

article.title: Choose a targeted Mac maintenance task before scheduling Pilot
article.primaryIntent: Help a Cocktail user separate a cache/log maintenance job from investigating storage that keeps growing, before choosing an automated routine.
article.leadDirection: Choose the OS-matched Cocktail edition and a specific documented task, not a blanket optimize routine. If the problem is recurring storage growth, first identify what is growing; maintenance and attribution are different jobs.
outline: After the lead: permitted Cocktail task-panel image with version caveat; currently blocked.
Match macOS to the documented edition; do not assume native Apple silicon support.
Separate cache/log maintenance from indexes, snapshots and system-setting changes; use only relevant task evidence, not a run-all tutorial.
Use a decision checklist: known rebuildable cache versus unexplained growth versus a specific system-setting problem; check backups and regeneration costs.
Explain Pilot's documented schedule without inventing exact approval or post-quit behavior.
Show current-source Breathing Room Space example; disclose we build it, preview/runtime/hosted limitations and why source-level investigation may fit.
Finish with a bounded choice, official help links and concise comparison link.
article.interactionPass: Decision checklist, not an arbitrary code demo: OS edition matched? Known disposable/rebuildable data? Backup and rebuild cost understood? Need routine maintenance or attribution/history? No execution or deletion controls.
article.length: Earned depth, approximately 1000–1400 words; no padding or fabricated FAQ.
article.distinctness: Workflow is task/edition/schedule selection, not a renamed product comparison or universal Mac optimization claim. No keyword-volume/SERP demand study performed.
